paragraphs.text: Good morning Tom, Jennie, Marcus – thank you for making time for us today. (Pause.)

Warren Buffett is often quoted as saying that it takes twenty years to build a reputation and five minutes to ruin it. Marcus, you carry Meridian’s reputation in front of customers every day. Over the next six months, as mobility moves into the EGW sub-brand, that trust either carries over or it is at risk.

When Tom and I spoke recently, three things stood out. First, Meridian is retiring its corporate mobile brand and moving all mobility into the EGW sub-brand – which means a brand-new Salesforce platform for CRM, assisted ordering and self-service, integrated with Siebel, Oracle and BRM.
Siebel has served Meridian for so long that it deserves a long-service award. Our job is to make sure its next chapter goes smoothly. (Pause.)
Second, the clock is tight: roughly six months, with a contractual commitment to be live by June-27.
Third – and this is what matters most – the stakes are your customers. Any gap from prospect to cash means disruption, churn and up to $3.54 billion of revenue at risk.

Marcus, in plain terms: this is the platform your customers will see and your teams will sell on. Your priority is simple: no customer lost in the move, revenue protected and the brand intact. Jennie, yours is zero disruption and green SLAs across every vendor. Tom, yours is a next-gen platform for Meridian’s future business model. Today is about showing how we can deliver all three.

Here is how we will use the time. Sushant, our Delivery and Innovation Lead, will show how AI-led delivery can reduce risk and speed this up. Neeti, who leads a peer telco program, will share a real story of what we did for a similar client’s customers. Suryakant, our Market Lead, will bring it together with one clear recommendation. And Aryama, our Client Engagement Lead, will keep plenty of room for your questions.

By the end, we hope to agree one simple next step – an initial assessment with you and your key stakeholders, so we can build a plan together that protects your customers and meets the June-27 commitment.
With that, over to Sushant.

deliveryTips: Pause after the Buffett quote and after the Siebel joke. Say the joke deadpan, and look at Jennie.
Keep “often quoted as saying”: the line is widely attributed to Buffett, but its exact origin is debated.

paragraphs.text: Every Siebel estate has a ghost: a rule nobody remembers writing, still running quietly, and occasionally billing. (Pause. Smile.)

Tom, Jennie, Marcus, you are standing up a new Salesforce platform in six months, on top of systems nobody has fully written down. In plain terms: nobody has a complete list of the rules that decide what each customer is charged.

We saw the same with Daniel, Head of Digital Delivery at a large Asia-Pacific mobile operator, whom we met at MWC Shanghai in June 2026. He had 26 weeks, 1,400 order workflows and 600 pricing rules. The plan allowed five weeks to document them; the work needed twelve. Seven weeks that did not exist.

More analysts or a straight rebuild would not work: the knowledge was buried in code written by people who had left. Grace Hopper warned that the most dangerous phrase in the language is “We’ve always done it this way.” Then a billing analyst found, by accident, an undocumented discount that would have put 50,000 customers on the wrong bill. (Pause.) Marcus, that is 50,000 customers, under a brand you are about to launch. If one rule was hiding, how many more?
We built four things.
First, our AI assistant, GenWizard, reads the old systems and drafts every rule in plain business language, linked to its source. Daniel’s experts accepted, edited or rejected each one.

Second, data you can trust. We reconcile customer, order and billing data across the systems before anything moves. The AI runs inside your environment, your people review every output, and no data is lost or exposed.
Third, myWizard gives every vendor one control tower: scope, dependencies and test status, with a clear RACI and a speed target for each activity.
Fourth, speed. Thin releases with automated quality checks, so problems surface in month one, not at go-live.
For Daniel, discovery took five weeks, not twelve. His own architect decided which rules to keep. The AI decided nothing.

Marcus, what does that mean for your customers? The right bill, from day one, under the new brand. Tom, you do not need more people to meet June 2027; you need to see your estate sooner. Jennie, you get a live view across every vendor.
So we would like to start with a two-week proof of concept on a sample of Meridian’s estate, inside your environment. Neeti will now share what happens when business and IT look at the same customer.

deliveryTips: Deliver the opening joke deadpan and wait for the smile. It sets up the hidden-rule idea that pays off later.
Slow down on the Hopper quote and look at Jennie; it is the point where Daniel’s plan has to change.

paragraphs.text: “What if Meridian could meet its June-27 commitment without asking customers to choose between continuity today and a better digital experience tomorrow?” Tom, Jennie, Marcus, that is the opportunity in front of you.
This is more than retiring a brand and implementing Salesforce. It is a chance to protect customer trust and revenue, and build Meridian’s digital foundation for growth.

In six months you must build Salesforce, integrate Siebel, Oracle and BRM, migrate mobility customers and coordinate multiple vendors. One failed customer journey could hit service and confidence, and up to $3.54 billion in revenue is exposed.

So the biggest opportunity is not Salesforce alone. It is one connected prospect-to-cash experience, with a control tower that gives everyone a common view of journeys, releases, dependencies and risk.

Marcus, this is where your world and Tom’s meet. Today, what Sales commits and what Service can deliver are not always the same. A plan sold as active in three hours that takes six is a broken promise, and the customer feels it. One shared view fixes that, and keeps your pricing and package decisions profitable once servicing costs are counted.

We have seen this work. In a comparable Salesforce program, Accenture supported more than 1,000 users across APAC, EMEA and the US, with 16-week releases over 18 months. The lesson was simple: do not wait for the final migration to find out whether it works. Validate early, learn quickly and scale with confidence.

For Meridian, we would first identify the customer journeys that simply cannot fail. Then make every dependency visible. Then deliver thin, testable releases with automated quality checks, under one-team governance across Meridian and its partners.

The value goes beyond implementation: revenue and retention protected, better order and SLA performance, more self-service, faster launch of new plans. That is Value 360, and it asks for a shift from vendor-by-vendor to shared outcomes.

That brings me to the second question: “The question isn’t whether Meridian can go live by June-27. The real question is: can Meridian use June-27 to change what becomes possible on June-28?” Success is reaching June-28 with customers protected, employees empowered, risks under control, and a platform ready for growth.

So our recommendation is simple: start with a focused two-week assessment. Bring together business, technology, data, operations and your key vendors. Identify the critical journeys, agree the value scorecard, and select the first early-validation release. Let’s not wait for go-live to find out whether it works. Let’s prove what matters most, early.

deliveryTips: Pause after each of the two questions; they are the spine of the speech.
Point to the credential slide when you say “We have seen the value of that approach before.”

paragraphs.text: Tom, Jennie, Marcus, you have heard our story. Let me finish with what it means and what we propose.

Our commitment is simple: help you move all mobility operations into the EGW brand within six months, while protecting customer relationships, keeping service running and building a platform for future growth.

Marcus, you will ask: so what does this mean for my customers? It means they keep the service they trust, get the right bill, and meet a better digital experience as the new brand arrives, without being asked to choose between the two.
With Accenture you gain a partner focused not only on delivery milestones, but on the business outcomes they must enable: customers kept, revenue protected, brand intact.

Here is what we would build: a workable solution, not Salesforce for its own sake, though we will show you why Salesforce is the fastest route. One connected journey from first enquiry to payment. Sales and Service working to one definition of “committed”. Clean data across your systems, with AI used safely inside your environment. And one team across every vendor, with a clear RACI and a speed target for each activity.

Our recommendation is simple. Before we commit to the full roadmap, start with a focused initial assessment. It answers your hardest questions with evidence: what this costs, whether six months is feasible, and where the risks sit. At the end you will have prioritized risks and dependencies, validated assumptions, a high-level roadmap and clear next steps.
The next step is just as simple. Tom, align on scope and agree a short window. Marcus, nominate one commercial owner for the customer journeys. Jennie, nominate your technology lead.
Tom, Marcus, Jennie, would you be comfortable sponsoring this initial assessment, so we can build a foundation you can trust for your six-month move to EGW?

deliveryTips: Pause before the final question, then stop talking and let Tom answer.
Say the assessment window and dates out loud once the team has agreed on them.
